H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper explicitly designs a double-layer FSM: top layer has general path/special path, and bottom layer has six driving behavior states.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions/events depend on lane validity, vehicle/obstacle detection, entry/exit points, speed <= 2 m/s, and distance guards d1 < dth / d1 > dth.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: States generate local reference points, vary speed with the front vehicle, shift reference points for lane change, adjust speed near ramps/intersections, and check obstacles.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No explicit fault, rollback, emergency-stop, or recovery transition is specified; emergency scenarios are mentioned only as future work.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Special-path semantics are split across map-building details, top-layer FSM road-type switching, and bottom-layer special-path behavior.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Domain terms such as following, overtaking, buffer adjustment, and special path are mostly explained with their local rules in the paper.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The bottom-layer state list is followed in the same subsection by per-state prose describing the main behavior/action of each state.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The FSM guards are mainly event or threshold conditions; no single transition guard combines multiple variables with arithmetic or Boolean composition.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: The upper special-path mode changes allowed behavior by disallowing overtaking, while the lower layer still manages driving behavior states.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: There is no from-any-state fault or recovery escape rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: The model has a shallow two-layer FSM with an initial bottom-layer structured-driving state, but no deep pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Numeric guard conditions such as speed <= 2 m/s and d1 < dth / d1 > dth give a weak expression-checking advantage.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No explicit global forced transition or parent-level continuous monitor applying to three or more substates is declared.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The controller outputs abstract planning actions such as local reference-point generation, trajectory generation, lane-reference shifting, and speed adjustment.

key_nl_quotes: A double-layer finite state machine is devised to plan driving behavior under different driving scenarios.
Overtaking is divided into lane change, overtake, and lane return, with d1 < dth and d1 > dth distance conditions.
one_line_pitch: A two-layer autonomous-bus behavior supervisor with nested road modes, six lower driving states, numeric driving guards, and abstract trajectory/reference-point actions stresses hierarchy and action recovery beyond an Umple-style baseline.
rationale: This is a strong stress-test because hierarchy is central to the paper's contribution: road-type supervision sits above concrete behavior states. The action signal is also rich, since states determine reference points, speed behavior, lane shifts, obstacle checking, and trajectory generation rather than merely emitting simple commands. Guards are meaningful but mostly threshold/event based, and the sample lacks explicit fault recovery, so its strength is hierarchy plus actions rather than global recovery.
